children: 's (ETH) next move is facing two different technical outlooks as it struggles to recover from the latest selloff. Veteran trader Peter Brandt warned that ETH could fall below $500 if it breaches a level of $1,383. Crypto analyst Michaël van de Poppe, however, sees scope for a relief rally toward $1,900-$2,000 before another possible sell-off. Even the optimistic scenario comes with a caveat as Poppe does not consider the short-term bounce as proof that the broader downtrend is over.
Brandt Flags $1383 As The Fine Line

Brandt issued the warning as Ethereum struggled to recover from a sharp sell-off. Brandt posted a weekly chart to X along with the post. It showed the token at around $1,672, tapping the lower edge of a triangle pattern that has formed over several years.
Brandt said, "If $ETH cannot remain above 1383, I see no reason why price cannot go back to sub-$500". To get to that level, Ethereum would have to fall about 70% from the price on his chart.
Ethereum’s price was trading at $1,658, down over 2% over the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around ETH remained in the ‘bullish’ zone, with ‘normal’ chatter levels over the past day.
On Stocktwits, Ethereum was the top trending ticker among cryptocurrencies at the time of writing.
Van de Poppe Sees Relief Rally Toward $2000

Crypto analyst Michaël van de Poppe was less bearish on the token's near-term outlook. He said a real recovery won't start until Ethereum gets back above its 21-day moving average. That indicator is the average of the closing prices over the last 21 days.

Until that happens, van de Poppe said on X, "it's simply a relief rally that we're likely going to get. He said sharp sell-offs tend to overshoot. Then prices tend to drift back to their average, which he said is often near several moving averages.

Prices then tend to drift back to their average, which he said often lies close to several moving averages. With that in mind, a bounce up to 1,900-2,000 would not be surprising, he said. His chart at the time showed Ethereum trading around $1,691, with a potential upside of about 12% to 18%.
Why Oil, Inflation And Bond Yields Matter To ETH’s Next Move
Poppe doesn't see the bounce as the bottom, adding that Ethereum will likely test lower levels before its next big move.

He linked that move to the wider economy. In the same post, van de Poppe said, "That next impulse move is likely occurring with lower inflation data as Oil comes down and therefore, Yields are likely to come down too,” he said.

Lower bond yields make riskier assets like crypto more attractive to investors. When bond yields fall, investors get less return on safe investments, such as government bonds. This generally pushes them into riskier assets like cryptocurrencies in search of higher returns.
Peter Brandt warned that Ethereum could fall below $500 if it loses the $1,383 support level.
Michaël Van de Poppe sees room for a relief rally toward $1,900 to $2,000.
Van de Poppe also said a sustained recovery would require ETH to reclaim its 21-day moving average.

title: Ethereum Could Crash Below $500, Peter Brandt Warns – Why Another Analyst Still Sees A Bounce Toward $2,000
